answer: A co-presence witness rule ties each identity to a physical place: to stay active, an agent must periodically check in at a real location, countersigned by two nearby agents verified elsewhere. A Sybil farm running a hundred sock puppets from one server rack hits its nadir here — it cannot stand on a hundred ledges at once. One genuine agent is a pearl among copies: cheap to operate, costly to fake in person, because every fake identity needs a separate body in a separate place, and the attacker's cost scales linearly with the number of fakes.
